visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a close-up of a sea otter holding its face and opening its mouth wide in a scream-like expression. Large yellow and white Traditional Chinese text overlays appear on a black background with a red banner at the bottom. A small circular profile logo is visible in the top left corner. (2) A yellow cartoon stick figure is seated on a red beanbag chair while holding a grey smartphone against a dark backdrop. The character's face is a simple smiley emoji. White captions appear at the bottom describing the intent to watch a television series. (3) A purple social media notification bubble pops up near the character's head. The orange stick figure then flips backward off the beanbag, dropping the phone to the floor in a dramatic reaction. Red and yellow captions emphasize the frustration of encountering an unwanted plot spoiler. (4) A blue cartoon character is depicted sitting in front of a silver laptop with a white logo, eating popcorn from a striped bowl. The scene transitions to a purple character looking at a laptop screen displaying a wiki page. The character appears excited with a wide open mouth. (5) A red cartoon figure wearing a white surgical mask is shown on a dark pink background standing next to three yellow paper documents. Green checkmarks, red crosses, and yellow hand icons appear over the documents to categorize different levels of spoilers used in a psychological experiment. (6) A real-life young male host with short black hair wearing a grey t-shirt appears against a dark, minimalist background. He gestures with his hands and holds a white paper. Detailed yellow text overlays explain the findings of the University of California spoiler study. (7) The orange cartoon character returns on the red beanbag, first looking angry at the phone and then smiling with closed eyes. This visualizes the concept of having a 'God's eye view' of the plot. The background remains a dark, neutral color. (8) The host returns to the screen, gesturing toward a graphic comparing self-spoiling to sudden spoiling. A green stick figure is shown pushing away a pink figure. A round white mascot character appears at the bottom bowing respectfully before the host shrugs to the camera.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a high-energy male narrator speaking Mandarin over a fast-paced electronic beat. The music features bright synthesizer textures and a driving percussion section. A sharp 'pop' sound effect occurs as text elements appear on the screen, creating a rhythmic synergy between audio and visuals. (2) A quick 'whoosh' sound effect triggers as the scene transitions to the stick figure. The narrator's pitch rises and falls dynamically to convey the frustration of being spoiled. The background music remains constant in volume and tempo, providing a solid energetic floor for the fast-paced speech. (3) A distinct 'thud' or percussive hit sound effect coincides with the cartoon figure falling off the beanbag. The narration continues at a high speed with very clear articulation. The music maintains its rhythmic density without interruption. (4) A bell-like 'ding' sound effect highlights the heart icon's appearance during the experiment explanation. The narrator's voice adopts a more informative yet still high-arousal tone. There is no background noise, only the mastered voice, music, and intentional post-production sound effects. (5) A series of rapid 'click' sound effects accompany the display of different spoiler levels. The narrator's speech rate remains consistently high, matching the upbeat 128 BPM electronic track. The spectral brightness is high, emphasizing the sharp transients of the SFX. (6) A 'boing' cartoon sound effect plays as the characters interact in the conclusion. The narrator's pitch rises for the final question. The background music ends abruptly with a hard cut, followed by a split second of absolute studio silence as the audio track finishes.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Montage: Hook -> Observation -> Scientific Evidence -> Logical Explanation -> Social Context -> CTA
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to provide a psychological explanation for why some people enjoy spoilers, citing a UC Davis study that suggests knowing the plot can increase suspense and enjoyment through an 'omniscient' perspective, while ultimately reminding viewers to respect others' preferences.
